impacts.claim: v1.0 adds an end-to-end rescue orchestrator that composes whitebox, safety, diagnosis, recovery planning, Linear import preparation, proactive PM routing, and release evidence.
impacts.evidence: The approved v1.0 success standard requires a messy mature project to become understandable and manageable end to end.
impacts.next_verification: Review the final AIPOS-052 through AIPOS-059 feature-to-code and feature-to-evidence matrix.

impacts.claim: The rescue workflow remains Python standard-library only and composes existing local scanners without installing project dependencies or accessing production.
impacts.evidence: Existing whitebox, safety, traceability, release, and upgrade tools use standard-library implementations with offline fixtures.
impacts.next_verification: Compile every source/template tool and run rescue fixtures in an isolated temporary repository.

impacts.claim: Rescue evidence may identify credentials, private project memory, settings, data boundaries, and contradictions, so outputs must stay sanitized, path-confined, and free of raw values or source lines.
impacts.evidence: SECURITY_BOUNDARY and the existing scanners prohibit matched values, source lines, environment values, and file contents in evidence.
impacts.next_verification: Test secret-bearing fixtures, output traversal, OS-self exclusion, forbidden input fields, and deterministic sanitized receipts.

impacts.claim: Startup, rescue protocol, workflow, quality gates, Linear handoff, examples, and operator prompts must present one coherent rescue path in English and Chinese.
impacts.evidence: START_HERE currently requires users to manually sequence several phases and tools.
impacts.next_verification: Run strict validator and review the installed-package 60-second rescue path.

impacts.claim: The v1.0 success standard requires deterministic end-to-end tests for messy project evidence, routing, safety blocking, idempotent reruns, output freshness, and one-Project Linear drafts.
impacts.evidence: Train A and Train B established focused unit tests, deterministic packages, extracted-package tests, and real workflow dogfood as release gates.
impacts.next_verification: Run focused rescue tests, the full source suite, deterministic package comparison, and the full extracted-package suite.

impacts.claim: Only the Owner can judge whether the generated diagnosis, risks, roadmap, ownership queues, and next action make a previously messy project controllable.
impacts.evidence: The v1.0 success standard is an end-to-end human outcome and AI Project OS forbids self-acceptance.
impacts.next_verification: Prepare one bilingual v1.0 UAT with explicit actions and expected results, then stop for Owner approval.

impacts.claim: Rescue planning must be read-only for product code and external systems by default; generated OS evidence must be branch-reviewable and removable without altering project behavior.
impacts.evidence: Existing policies require inspect-plan-approve boundaries, branch-based changes, protected memory, and human-controlled external writes and releases.
impacts.next_verification: Dogfood in isolated and real repositories, verify reruns are harmless, and confirm abandoning the branch removes only generated OS evidence.

test_plan: Compile all source and template Python tools.
Test dry-run inspection, authorized local plan writes, deterministic reruns, and stale-output verification.
Test OS-owned path exclusion so product evidence is not dominated by the installed OS package.
Test safety blocks, contradictions, missing target version, missing dependencies/tests/docs/CI, and human gate routing.
Test bilingual one-Project Linear draft records with Action Steps, Expected Result, Milestone, duplicate keys, and no remote mutation.
Run the full source suite, strict validator, staged/private safety gate, deterministic package build, and extracted-package suite.
uat_plan: Owner runs one rescue command in a representative messy mature project.
Owner verifies that diagnosis separates evidence, confidence, impact, contradictions, unknowns, and next verification.
Owner verifies that the recovery roadmap says what humans and Codex do next and what proves completion.
Owner verifies that the Linear package targets one Project and one Milestone and remains dry-run before approval.
Owner verifies that no secret value, source line, production action, external write, business Decision, UAT approval, or release happens automatically.
Owner gives an explicit pass or fail conclusion for v1.0.0.
rollout: Implement on codex/v1.0-internal-stable, keep rescue product/external operations read-only, dogfood and package through a Draft PR, then stop for explicit v1.0.0 Owner UAT before merge, tag, or Release.
rollback: Before release, abandon the v1.0 branch or remove generated rescue evidence. After release, reinstall immutable v0.8.0 on a dedicated branch while preserving local overrides, audit/Linear history, safety dispositions, discovery evidence, and private runtime context.
